rationale:
The subject `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read_source` has three obligations. It must resolve an outline item to its graph node. It must read the contents. It must record the observation as described by the cited `read_source.inputs`. The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[direct_source_reads_preserve_mapping_errors_and_record_only_successful_returns]` covers each of them. I did not read the implementation. The judgment rests on the test source.

- **Resolution failures.** Two addresses are tried: an unknown file (`unknown.txt`) and a known file with an unknown item (`source.txt` with `line[unknown]`). Each must return an "unsupported source item" error. The test then asserts that `dependencies()` is empty, that `reads == 0`, and that `read_nodes` is empty. So no read is attempted when resolution fails, and nothing is recorded.
- **Read failure after successful resolution.** With `fail_read = true`, the call returns the "prepared source read failed" error and `dependencies()` stays empty. This matches "failures record no successful observation".
- **Successful read.**
  - The returned contents are checked: `format()` equals "prepared contents".
  - The recorded dependency is asserted to be exactly `Dependency::Node("source-node", returned.fingerprint())`. That checks both the mapped node identity and the fingerprint of the supplied contents.
  - `read_nodes` is asserted to be `["source-node","source-node"]`. The failed read and the successful read both reached the node that the item resolved to.
- **Staleness.** The context is finished into a record, and `record.is_current` is true. After the node's text is changed, `is_current` is false. This covers the rule that the dependency becomes stale when the node's fingerprint changes.

The other parts of the cited `read_source.inputs` text are not part of this subject's own obligations. These are the agent-delivery recording, the standalone outline parser recording nothing, and the rule that the mapping cannot return an untracked read. Agent delivery and the standalone parser are not part of the direct `read_source` call. The untracked-read rule is handled by the source-mapping requirement. The `public_api.rs` test is unrelated to this behavior and contributes nothing here. I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that the main test would accept.

text: Resolve an outline item to its graph node, read the contents, and record the observation under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_source.inputs`.
pub fn read_source(&self, item: &OutlineId) -> Result<D::NodeContent, D::Error>;
A successful source read records the mapped node's identity and the fingerprint
record when returning the contents; agent reads record when delivering them.
The dependency becomes stale when that node's fingerprint changes. The source
mapping cannot return an untracked successful read. Calling the standalone
outline parser directly records no graph dependency; a tracked node read must
enclose its use when its contents contribute to an assessment.
